newsitem.title: USA: Apogee's stock drops on report of Medicare billings review. [CORRECTED 19:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Apogee's stock drops on report of Medicare billings review. [CORRECTED 19:05 GMT]

text.p: The stock of Apogee Inc., one of the largest providers of outpatient mental health services in the country, fell more than 22 percent Tuesday after the company reported sharply lower earnings and said federal authorities were reviewing certain billings made by a subsidiary.

The company reported a lower net profit for the three months ended Sept. 30 of $280,000, or 3 cents a share, from $1.02 million, or 11 cents a share, despite a 9 percent increase in revenues to $19.3 million from $17.7 million. (Corrects to make clear Apogee made a profit, not a loss, in the latest quarter).
Apogee fell $1.50 to $5.25 in midday on the Nasdaq market, where the stock was one of the biggest percentage losers.

The stock dropped after Apogee reported substantially lower third-quarter profits and said the Department of Justice and the Department of Health and Human Services were reviewing certain Medicare and related billings by a subsidiary.

Apogee said it could not predict the outcome of the review, when it would be completed or its potential impact on the company's earnings. It added that it did not expect the final outcome to have a material adverse impact on its financial condition.

"The review is a civil matter relating to billings for services to Medicare patients in long-term care facilities in the state of Florida from Jan. 1, 1994, through mid-1995," Apogee said in a statement.
Apogee, which operates inpatient and outpatient mental health group practices, said it was fully cooperating with the review but did not provide any further information on the government probe.

For the first nine months, Apogee said its net income fell to $1.2 million, or 12 cents a share, from $4.1 million, or 43 cents a share, despite an 18 percent increase in revenues to $59.4 million from $50.3 million.
